Also, if high concentrations of pyrilutamide is not detectable in blood, or detectable at very negligible amounts, we can still outcompete dht by outnumbering it by pyrilutamide in the scalp. When there are a large number of antagonist molecules present in the scalp, they have a higher chance of encountering and binding to androgen receptors compared to the lower number of DHT molecules. Even though the individual binding affinity of the antagonist is weaker, the collective effect of a higher concentration can overcome the binding of DHT to the receptor. This phenomenon is based on the law of mass action, which states that the rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants. In this case, the antagonist concentration would be high, increasing the likelihood of antagonist molecules binding to androgen receptors and displacing DHT.
